title: Decimal Division Word Problems: Full and Partial Groups
intro: Use a measurement model to explain a quotient that includes part of a group.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Mark full groups along the total length or amount. Compare the leftover part with the size of one whole group.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Two full groups use 14 units. The remaining 3.5 units are half of a 7-unit group. The total is therefore 2 + 0.5 = 2.5 groups.

The empty dashed half is a reference showing the size of a complete third group. It is not extra material and is not included in the total of 17.5.

Ask your student

What fraction of one group is still left?

If your student needs help

If the student drops the partial group, include it in a multiplication check of the total.
